newsitem.title: GERMANY: German barge traffic flows slightly reduced.
newsitem.headline: German barge traffic flows slightly reduced.

text.p: Closure of the Elbe and Oder rivers and estuaries due to high water levels leaves most of German barge trade intact, the shippers organisation BDB (Bundesverband der Deutschen Binnenschiffahrt) said.
"Current waterway closures take out only a few percent of total traffic volumes," managing director Gerhard von Haus said in response to an enquiry.
River banks and flood walls have been pressured by torrential rainfall this month.
Shipping has been suspended on the two rivers connecting Germany with Poland and the Czech republic.
Von Haus said the closures did not extend to key mineral oil routes while incoming supplies from Poland were mostly construction material.
The share of grains, feedstuffs, ores or metals in the blocked traffic volumes was also small.
BDB represents some 3,000 vessels in the 500-3,000 tonne category, the bulk of the German-owned inland barge fleet.

Officials at the German compound feed industry association (FFMI) said some southern European shipments of feed grain and other raw materials to the west may have been disrupted when Danube shipping was suspended in Austria on Sunday.
On Monday, the Passau-Linz route was reopened but an eastern stretch running to the Slovak border remained closed.
